 Judgment

1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 02.05.2019 passed in MVC.No.39/2018 by Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Arsikere, (for short the 'Tribunal') the present appeal is filed by the petitioner therein for enhancement of compensation awarded.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The case of the petitioner is that on 20.10.2017 at about 7.15 p.m., the petitioner was standing on the left side of the road in front of his house at Nandihalli village and at that time, a lorry bearing registration No. KA-07/A-0322 being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against him and that the said lorry was duly insured with respondent No.2 - Insurance company and because of the accident he suffered the following injuries:
i. Crush injury right knee with complex open fracture of right knee.
ii. Crush injury of right leg with severe soft tissue loss.

iii. Fracture of right patella.
 iv. Abrasion over forehead.
 v. Abrasion over right shoulder.
The tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.1,82,924/- which is not sufficient and hence the present appeal is filed.
4. The Insurance company justifies the order passed by the tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

2 5.
It is seen that the petitioner was 7 years old when he met with an accident.
He has suffered a permanent body disability of 22% to the whole body.
It is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of motor vehicle accident.

However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MASTER MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED & ANOTHER reported in AIR 2014 SC 736, in paragraph 12 has held as under:
"12.

entities.text: MASTER MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED & ANOTHER reported in AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High courts,
we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; up to 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90% , it should be Rs.6 lakhs.
For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Rs.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
In the instant case, the disability is to the tune of 18%.
Appellant had a longer period of hospitalization for about two months causing also inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents."

6. Thus, in the instant case, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards permanent physical disability, Rs.33,000/- towards discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during period of hospitalization, as a minimum of 3 months has to be considered as laid up period of the petitioner requiring parental attention and loss of income to the parents during the said period and the accident being of the year 2017 and the notional income as per lok- adalath chart of the parent would be Rs.11,000/- per month and a sum of Rs.45,424/- towards medical expenses as determined by the tribunal as per actual bill and also a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses as determined by the tribunal.
Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.4,03,424/- as against Rs.1,82,924/- awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,20,500/.
Given the bank rate of interest, I am of the opinion it would be appropriate to award interest @ 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation.

8. Hence, the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.2,20,500/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition before the tribunal till realization which shall be over and above what has been awarded by the tribunal and respondent No.2 -Insurance company shall satisfy the same within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
